description:
The gate definition and preset arms build payloads inline and substitute gate-specific fallback codes. This moves them to library handlers with typed responses.

## Background

In `crates/jit/src/main.rs`, `GateCommands::{Define, Update, Remove, Add, List, Show}` and `PresetCommands::{List, Show, Apply, Create}` build bodies with `json!` (`define`, `remove`, `add`, `preset list` with an inline count, `preset apply`, `preset create`) or construct `GateListResponse` inline. Under `--json` they report failures with call-site codes: `GATE_ERROR` (exit 6) for `define`, `update`, `list` and `fail`-style paths, `GATE_NOT_FOUND`/`GATE_ERROR` in `add`, `PRESET_ERROR` (exit 3) in the preset arms, and `resolve_gate_key_for` prints `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and exits. `define --env` parse errors call `exit(2)` on the human path only. `preset apply` with per-gate errors builds an inline `JsonError` with a chosen `failure_code` and exits. Most of these leaves fall back to `CommandResponse` in the schema.

A handler in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/` takes its parsed arguments and a `CommandContext` (the executor and the `OutputMode { json, quiet }`) and returns `anyhow::Result<Outcome<R>>`; one registration per group generates the group's dispatch and its schema response lookup. Success responses are types defined in the output module (`crates/jit/src/output/`) or output constructors wrapping a command-layer result, each deriving `JsonSchema` and a human rendering; list payloads are `ListEnvelope<K, T, E>` instantiations; failures are returned as errors that `jit::output::failure::classify` maps to one code and exit status; a non-zero findings result is `Outcome`'s findings variant, rendered under `--json` as the failure envelope with the report in `error.details` and its registered code as the exit status.

On main, `run()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` parses the arguments and calls `dispatch()` in `main.rs`, which holds the command match; the arms and inline code this issue places in `run()` live in `dispatch()`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `run()` dispatches `gate define|update|remove|add|list|show` and `gate preset list|show|apply|create` to handlers in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/gate.rs`, and `main.rs` keeps no arm body or `resolve_gate_key_for`.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each leaf returns its registered response type, list payloads are `ListEnvelope` instantiations, and the schema names a typed response for every one of them.
- [hard] REQ-03: The handlers return failures as errors with no substituted code or `std::process::exit`; tests assert that a `gate define` failure classified as something other than `GATE_ERROR` reports its classified code and exit on both paths, and that an invalid `define --env` reports `INVALID_ARGUMENT` exit 2 on both paths.
- [hard] REQ-04: `gate preset apply` with per-gate errors returns a findings outcome rendered as the failure envelope with its report in `error.details`.
- [hard] REQ-05: Where a leaf's exit codes change, its rows in `CommandSchema::generate_command_exit_codes` (`crates/jit/src/schema.rs`) state the new codes and `docs/reference/exit-codes.md` is regenerated.
- [hard] REQ-06: Human output, success payloads and exit codes of these leaves are otherwise unchanged, and the existing suites pass without weakened assertions.

## Decisions

- D-01: REQ-06's unchanged human output excludes the per-gate error list of `gate preset apply`: as a findings outcome (REQ-04) its report prints on stdout and its message on stderr through the uniform emitter, where the old arm printed the list on stderr (steward ruling, 2026-11-04, as for the uniform findings rule).

## Notes

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`; inventories with function and arm citations: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md`.
title: Gate definition and preset commands move to library handlers
